instructions: Rinse the lentils in a sieve and pick out any small stones. Finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. Mince the 2 garlic cloves and finely chop the leaves from 1 sprig of rosemary.

Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium. Add the onion, carrots, celery and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and see-through. Don't rush this part. It's where the flavor starts.
Add the garlic, rosemary and 1 tbsp tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the paste darkens a shade.
Add the lentils, the 4 cups of broth and 1 cup of water. Turn the heat to high until it boils, then turn it down to medium-low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes, until the lentils are almost tender.
Add the pasta, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender. If it gets too thick, add a splash of water.
Take the pot off the heat and let it sit for 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve in bowls with a little extra black pepper. For lunches, cool it and pack it into containers. It keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and gets thicker each day, so stir in a splash of water when you reheat it.
method_notes: The Pasta Project version is the lead: a soffritto, tomato paste and rosemary, lentils simmered first, then pasta cooked in the same pot. I used its ratios scaled to 4, with vegetable broth in place of part of the water. Well Seasoned Studio adds pancetta, canned tomatoes and a Parmesan rind and keeps 4 days in the fridge; I left those out for a lunch-sized version. The lead shows 5 stars from 66 votes (visible rating). Both note leftovers thicken, which is why the last step says to loosen with water.
